title: Given an array of daily prices, find the maximum profit from a single buy and a single later sell. If no profit is possible, return 0.
shortTitle: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock — track min price and max profit

s1_definition.profdef: Scan prices once, maintaining the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit achievable by selling on the current day (current price minus the running minimum). Update both each day; the answer is the maximum profit, defaulting to zero when prices only fall. This is a single-pass O(n) greedy/DP hybrid using O(1) space.
s1_definition.analogy: A trader at National Bank of India wants to buy a share on one day and sell it on a later day for the biggest gain. As you walk through the days, you remember the cheapest price so far and ask, "if I sell today, how much do I make?" You keep the best such answer.
s1_definition.oneliner: Track the lowest price so far and the best sell-today profit; the maximum of those profits is the answer.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Scan prices once, maintaining the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit achievable by selling on the current day (current price minus the running minimum). Update both each day; the answer is the maximum profit, defaulting to zero when prices only fall. This is a single-pass O(n) greedy/DP hybrid using O(1) space.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A trader at National Bank of India wants to buy a share on one day and sell it on a later day for the biggest gain. As you walk through the days, you remember the cheapest price so far and ask, "if I sell today, how much do I make?" You keep the best such answer.

**One line to remember:** Track the lowest price so far and the best sell-today profit; the maximum of those profits is the answer.

sections.s2_technical:
Initialize the minimum price to the first day and max profit to zero. Each day, update the minimum if the price is lower, else compute the profit of selling today and update the max profit. For example: `minPrice = Math.min(minPrice, p); maxProfit = Math.max(maxProfit, p - minPrice);`.

Because you only ever sell after buying at the running minimum, every candidate respects the buy-before-sell order. If prices only decline, max profit stays zero, correctly signaling no profitable trade.

The time is O(n) and the space is O(1). A senior nuance is that the multi-transaction variant (Stock II) sums every positive day-to-day difference, and the with-cooldown variant becomes a small state machine, so recognizing which variant you face dictates the technique.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India's trading desk, a strategy buys one share and sells it later for the maximum single-trade gain over a price history. This is exactly how Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock works.

Problem 2 — You can only sell after you buy, and if the market only falls you make no trade. This is exactly why the running minimum precedes each sell and the default profit is zero.

The mini-project builds a `SingleTradeProfitFinder`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input prices are seven, one, five, three, six, four.

Step 1: Day one sets the minimum to seven and profit to zero.

Step 2: Day two price one is lower, so the minimum drops to one.

Step 3: Day three price five gives profit four; day four price three gives profit two, so max profit stays four.

Step 4: Day five price six gives profit five, the new best; day six price four gives profit three.

Step 5: The maximum single-trade profit is five, from buying at one and selling at six.

```text
2026-10-27T01:00:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Single-Trade Profit Finder (Buy/Sell Stock)
2026-10-27T01:00:00Z [INFO] Max single-trade profit = 5
2026-10-27T01:00:00Z [INFO] Best = 5
```


sections.s6_takeaway:
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock for a single transaction is a clean single-pass algorithm. I walk through the prices maintaining two things: the lowest price seen so far, which is the best day to have bought, and the best profit I could lock in by selling on the current day, which is the current price minus that running minimum. Each day I either lower the minimum or update the maximum profit, and the answer is that maximum, defaulting to zero when the market only declines.

Because I always compute the sell profit against a minimum that occurred earlier in the scan, every candidate respects the buy-before-sell ordering automatically, so I never need to compare all pairs of days. It runs in linear time and constant space.

In my project at National Bank of India's trading desk, a strategy identified the maximum single-trade gain over a price history, and this running-minimum approach computed it in one pass over the live feed. I always clarify which variant is in play, because the multi-transaction version just sums every positive day-to-day move and the cooldown version becomes a small state machine, so naming the variant determines the right technique.
